caption: The drawing features a rectangular composition with a central scene framed in ornate gold scrollwork, depicting a group of people in colonial attire, and the date “1792.” Surrounding the central image are various objects and portraits: in the bottom left corner, a framed portrait of a man with laurel leaves around him, in the upper right corner, another portrait similarly adorned, in the top left a wreath with pink flowers encircles an image of a globe with “22” and a snake-like figure, and in the lower right, a wreath with pink flowers frames a building resembling the United States Capitol. Additionally, two smaller images of the Statue of Liberty, labeled “LIBERTY,” appear above and below the central scene. The background is filled with five-pointed white stars outlined in gray, containing abbreviations for U.S. state names, on alternating vertical stripes of pale pink and cream. The words “PLURIBUS UNUM” are interspersed among the stars. The overall color scheme is primarily gray, cream, pale pink, and brown, with green and pink accents in the floral wreaths. The artist’s signature, “F.A. Smallen,” appears in the bottom right corner.
title: Printed Cotton - Historical
